S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.

subtypes.Responsiveness to Extraneous Stimuli: Attention is immediately drawn to trivial and unimportant stimuli nearby (e.g., noise, movement).
subtypes.Frequent Task Switching: Unable to finish one task and constantly shifting attention to new things, starting multiple tasks simultaneously.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Unable to focus on any activity for long, with attention constantly being scattered.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

S041.name: Painful_Consequence_Behavior
S041.description: Excessive involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences.

subtypes.Unrestrained Buying Sprees: Spending excessive amounts of money or shopping recklessly to a degree that creates financial distress for self and family.
subtypes.Foolish Business Investments: Making rash business investments or ventures without sufficient review.
subtypes.Sexual Indiscretions: Engaging in indiscriminate or risky sexual behavior that is out of character.
subtypes.Impulsive Risky Behavior: Excessively dangerous or foolish behavior, such as reckless driving or drug use, without considering the consequences.

symptom.disease_info: Bipolar I Disorder is defined by the occurrence of at least one manic episode, typically involving a sustained period of elevated, expansive, or irritable mood with increased energy or activity and clinically significant impairment. Episodes may emerge in the context of life stress or disrupted routines, but the diagnosis is based on the syndrome and its functional impact rather than the stressor alone. It is distinguished from Bipolar II Disorder by the presence of full mania rather than hypomania, and from primary depressive or adjustment disorders by the episodic manic course.

patient.stressor: Hector’s episode developed during a forced move from his long-time house to a smaller place closer to family, after repairs and rising costs made staying put unrealistic. Within a month, the disruption of leaving his workshop, garden, and familiar church route fed a sustained surge of energy and irritable enthusiasm: he tried to coordinate the move, redesign the new garage, organize community events, and advise younger workers all at once, talking so continuously that family and coworkers struggled to interrupt him. His distractibility and escalating goal-directed plans became dangerous when he neglected safety steps at the materials-processing shop, made costly commitments for renovations without consulting his wife, and drove repeatedly between homes to retrieve misplaced items despite family objections. He received psychiatric care after a workplace safety incident and a family confrontation led to an emergency evaluation, where the month-long manic course and functional impairment were recognized.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: I’ve been feeling like everybody needs to either get on board with my plans or get out of my way, and I’ll go from joking and feeling ten feet tall to snapping at my wife or my boy over some little question.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: I can’t seem to sit in the chair more than a few minutes before I’m up sorting boxes, measuring the garage, loading tools, or heading back to the old place because my body feels like it’s got a motor in it.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.
S037.manifestation: Once I start explaining what needs doing, the words just keep coming, and my family says I talk over them so fast they can’t even tell me to stop.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.
S039.manifestation: At the shop or at home, one clank, one truck passing, or one tool out of place pulls me off what I’m doing, and pretty soon I’ve got five things started and none of them finished.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.
S040.manifestation: I’m here because everyone says I’ve been doing too much, but to me it feels like I’m the only one with enough drive to get the move handled, rebuild the new garage right, organize things at church, and still show the younger fellows at work how the job ought to be done.

S041.name: Painful_Consequence_Behavior
S041.description: Excessive involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences.
S041.manifestation: I put deposits down on garage work and equipment without talking it over with my wife, and I kept driving back and forth between the houses and rushing jobs at the plant even after people warned me I was taking chances.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I ended up getting pulled from work after a safety incident, and at home my wife and family stopped trusting me with decisions about money, driving, or the move because things had gotten out of hand.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about a month, since we were forced to start leaving the old house.
